bib.title: VizWiz Grand Challenge: Answering Visual Questions from Blind People

question: How do visual questions asked by blind people with phone photos and spoken questions differ from artificial VQA data, and how well do existing VQA and answerability algorithms handle them?
hypothesis: Existing VQA algorithms trained on artificial datasets will perform poorly on goal-oriented, naturally captured visual questions from blind people.
contributions: VizWiz, the first goal-oriented VQA dataset from a natural setting: 31,000+ visual questions from blind people with 10 crowdsourced answers each
Anonymisation and filtering process with a vulnerability taxonomy
Analysis of questions, images, answers and answerability
Benchmark of nine VQA methods and eight answerability predictors

method.summary: Blind users' photos and spoken questions from the VizWiz app were transcribed, filtered for privacy, and given 10 AMT answers each. Three published VQA models were evaluated off the shelf, fine-tuned and trained from scratch, plus eight answerability predictors.
method.task: visual question answering and answerability prediction on images from blind photographers

datasets.name: VizWiz
datasets.split: 20,000 train / 3,173 val / 8,000 test (approx 65/10/25); all results on test
datasets.source: 72,205 questions from the VizWiz app (May 2011 onward, 11,045 users); 48,169 from users who agreed to share; 14,796 (~31%) filtered; publicly released at vizwiz.org/data
datasets.preprocessing: Audio transcribed by AMT workers, spell-checked; images re-saved lossless to strip metadata; AMT PII round (4,626 removed), expert round (2,693 removed), 7,477 with under two words removed; answers lowercased, numbers to digits, punctuation/articles/filler words removed, spelling fixed

datasets.name: VQA v2.0
datasets.preprocessing: Used to train the three off-the-shelf models on the 3,000 most frequent answers; also the cross-dataset test set (Table 5)

models.name: Q+I (Goyal et al. [18] in Table 3; [24] in text)
Q+I+A (Kazemi and Elqursh [24] in Table 3; [18] in text)
FT variants of the three
models.architecture: fine-tuned on VizWiz, top 3,000 VizWiz answers
models.init_from: VQA v2.0 pre-trained model; last-layer rows copied for answers also in VQA v2.0, random otherwise

models.name: VizWiz-from-scratch variants of the three
models.architecture: random init, trained on VizWiz only, top 3,000 answers

models.name: Answerability models Q, C, I, Q+C, Q+I, FT[30], VizWiz[30], VQA[18]
models.architecture: Q/C: one-layer LSTM + softmax; I: ResNet-152 pool5 + softmax; Q+C and Q+I: concatenated features + softmax; captions from NeuralTalk2 pre-trained on MSCOCO captions

training.lr: 0.01, dropped to 0.001 after the first 10 epochs (fine-tuning)
training.epochs: 10 epochs at lr 0.01, then another 10 (VQA fine-tuning); 10 epochs (answerability)

other.scratch_hyperparameters: not stated for from-scratch VQA models beyond random init and 3,000 answers

inference.samples: single run per model; no seeds or variance reported

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: VQA accuracy of Antol et al. [8]

metrics.name: CIDEr, BLEU4, METEOR
metrics.definition: image description metrics from the COCO caption server, used because nearly half of answers exceed one word

metrics.name: Average precision (AP) and average F1
metrics.definition: AP is the area under the precision-recall curve for predicting a question is not answerable

metrics.name: Human accuracy
metrics.definition: Dataset split into 10 sets of one answer per question; one set scored against the other nine, for all 10 partitions

eval.protocol: All results on the 8,000-question test set; unanswerable means at least half of the 10 answers are 'unanswerable' or 'unsuitable image'

evidence.quote: which we refer to as Q+I [24], Q+I+A [18], and Q+I+BUA [6]

results.quote: We next collected answers for a final set of 31,173 vi- sual questions.
results.note: The quote line-break hyphen may fail the check; see the abstract's 'over 31,000'.

results.claim: About 28.63% of visual questions are unanswerable.
results.setup: At least half of the 10 answers are 'unanswerable' or 'unsuitable image'
results.quote: We find 28.63% of visual questions are not answerable.
results.note: Section 5.1 gives the 'unanswerable' answer-type share as 34.6% (Table 4 text); the paper does not reconcile the two.

results.claim: 28% of images were labelled unsuitable by at least two of 10 workers.
results.setup: At least two crowd workers answered 'unsuitable image'
results.quote: We found 28% of images were labelled as such.

results.claim: Off-the-shelf VQA v2.0 models score about 0.14 accuracy on VizWiz test.
results.setup: Best of three models used as is, VizWiz test

results.claim: Fine-tuning the best model (bottom-up/top-down) reaches 0.475 accuracy.
Training from scratch on VizWiz alone gives accuracy 0.465 to 0.469, close to fine-tuning.

results.setup: One answer set scored against the other nine, 10 partitions

results.claim: Only 824 of the top 3,000 VizWiz answers are in the top 3,000 VQA 2.0 answers.
results.quote: only 824 out of the top 3,000 answers in VizWiz are included in the top 3,000 answers in VQA 2.0
results.note: Section 5.1 words it as 'in the dataset (i.e., VQA 2.0)'

results.claim: Models trained on VizWiz transfer poorly to VQA 2.0 test (0.218 to 0.318).
results.setup: Six VizWiz-trained models on VQA 2.0 test; 0.318 is FT [24]

results.claim: On unanswerable questions off-the-shelf models score 0.06-0.07 while fine-tuned reach 0.77-0.78 and scratch 0.80.
Q+I is the best answerability predictor at AP 71.7, versus 30.6 for the prior relevance method.
results.table: Table 6, row Q+I, column Average Precision

results.claim: Image alone gives AP 64, the largest single feature.
results.quote: the image provides the greatest predictive power (i.e., AP = 64)

results.claim: 27.88% of VizWiz questions start with a rare first word versus 13.4% for VQA 2.0.
results.setup: First word occurring in less than 5% of questions; VQA 2.0 on a random subset of 40,000

results.claim: Median question length is five words and mean 6.68.
results.quote: The median and mean question lengths are five and 6.68
results.note: Source text has 'ﬁve and 6.68' with ligature

results.claim: 67.32% of answers are one word; mean answer length 1.66 words.
Humans agree on an answer for 97.7% of visual questions under exact string matching.
results.note: 72.83% more than three agree; 15.5% exactly three; 9.67% exactly two

results.setup: Crowd round 4,626, expert round 2,693 (PII 895, location 377, indecent 55, complex scene 725, low quality 578, other 63), 7,477 missing question

limits: Answer types in Table 4: yes/no 4.80%, number 1.69%, other 58.91%, unanswerable 34.6%; the 34.6% differs from 28.63% without explanation.
Model citation labels are swapped between text (Q+I [24], Q+I+A [18]) and Table 3 (Q+I [18], Q+I+A [24]).
Filtering erred towards removing complex scenes and blurry images, so the released set may be easier than the raw stream (authors check with an average image).
No seeds, variance, hardware or from-scratch hyperparameters reported; 2018 models (no pre-trained vision-language models).
Answerability is judged by crowd workers, not blind users.
